title: protect.yml is detected by its exact filename and rerun last, after wait
answers: protect.yml rerun happens in the wrong order in retry
retry workflow protect workflow not rerun
how does retry.sh identify the protect workflow
body:
Invariant: retry.sh identifies the protect workflow by comparing the `workflow` field to the literal `protect.yml`, and reruns it only after the `wait` that follows the loop over other rows.
Where enforced: .github/workflows/retry.sh:runs (jq sets `workflow` to the basename of `.workflowRun.workflow.resourcePath` via `split("/")[-1]`) and the `while IFS=$'\t' read -r run_id workflow` loop that stores `protect_id`/`protect_workflow`, followed by `wait` and the deferred `rerun "$protect_id" "$protect_workflow"`.
What breaks if skipped: Comparing against a path (such as an endswith on "/protect.yml" after the field was changed to a bare filename) silently never matches, so protect is rerun as an ordinary parallel rerun or not at all. Renaming protect.yml requires updating the literal in retry.sh.
Constraints: The `workflow` value is a filename only, so comparisons must use filenames, not paths. Only one protect row is tracked (`protect_id` is a single variable); the reason for deferring it is not stated in the diff.
applies: Applies to workflow-name matching and rerun ordering in .github/workflows/retry.sh; does not cover which runs the jq filter selects for rerun.
says: The protection check does not rerun after renaming the merge validation configuration.
Renaming the protection workflow causes it to run out of order during retries.
Automatic retries fail to detect the protection check and run it in parallel.
Why did changing the merge check name break the deferred retry sequence?
search: Workflow matching in .github/workflows/retry.sh identifies the protection job by exact filename protect.yml before deferring its rerun until after wait. Applies to .github/workflows/retry.sh:runs and the while loop reading run_id and workflow, which expects a bare filename from jq. Comparing against full paths fails silently, renaming protect.yml requires updating the script literal, and only a single protect row is tracked.
